name: Staging the decision record
summary: When a run ends, a human-approved decision is written as a YAML record under the run folder, ready to publish.

steps.label: Spot an approved decision
steps.human:
At the end of the run, the decision executor sees a completed decision that a human approved.

The reconstructed JSON projections come from the parsed YAML record docs/decisions/dec-ef8ddcb79d668a67.yaml; they are not a new API envelope or a replay of its historical execution. This predicate examines the same internal Decision; it creates no serialized verdict.

steps.label: Build the record
steps.human:
The record builder collects the question, options, criteria, evidence references (locators and hashes, no text), the ranking you saw, the precedents considered, and provenance: run id, Langfuse trace id, repository revision and versions. It refuses an approver who is not human or a missing approved_at.

Source: kernel/memory/builder.py and staging.py. Full building also consumes execution-context provenance and the option, criterion and evidence collections; examples show selected input/output fields only.

steps.label: Write it under the run folder
steps.human:
The file backend writes the YAML to <run_root>/runs/<run_id>/staged/decisions/<id>.yaml, never into the repository: during a run the kernel only reads the repository (ADR-060).

The same DecisionRecord is written as YAML. Python returns StagedRecord(decision_id, path), or None on write failure; there is no JSON staging receipt.

steps.label: Tell you how to publish
steps.human:
The run's result says "decision record staged: <path>" and gives the command python -m kernel decisions publish --run-id R. The /leafcutter skill shows you this and never publishes by itself.

Source: kernel/capabilities/decision/executor.py _stage. The notice is appended to CapabilityResult.limitations and output_payload.limitations (the decision report). <run_root> is an explicitly illustrative installation-path placeholder.

branches.condition: the decision was resolved by the host alone or has no human approval
branches.label: Nothing is staged
branches.human:
No record is written, so there is nothing to publish and no later run can find this decision as precedent.

The builder also refuses invalid records; a backend or failed write can keep nothing. stage_decision_record returns Python None without changing the decision result or creating a serialized error.
